captions.threads:
1/ Your focus didn't break. Your inputs broke it. And we've normalized this so thoroughly that feeling fragmented has become the baseline. I'm not being poetic here, I'm being observational. The human nervous system isn't designed for 47 simultaneous demand streams.

2/ Every notification, every open tab, every half-heard conversation in the next room, every email you didn't address, the thought about the thing you forgot, the awareness that someone might be waiting on you. These aren't minor distractions. They're active inputs that your brain has to process and suppress in real time. That's exhausting at a metabolic level.

3/ The actual move isn't productivity hacking. It's reducing inputs until your nervous system remembers what calm focus feels like. Close the tabs. Turn off the badges. Create actual space for silence. This isn't ascetic. This is functional. Your best work lives on the other side of saying no to most things.

4/ When you reduce inputs, something shifts. You're not white-knuckling your attention anymore. You're not fighting your biology. You're just thinking. And thinking clearly is rarer and more powerful than we've been told. https://vibrationofawesome.com/blog/boom/posts/reducing-inputs-to-restore-focus
